subject: biology
title: Decomposition and rate of decay
key_idea: Bacteria and fungi decay dead plants and animals. They decay faster when it is warm, moist and there is plenty of oxygen. Decay returns mineral ions to the soil, and its rate can be calculated from the change in mass over time.

blocks.text: (Separate science) Dead plants and animals are broken down by microorganisms. This section covers who does it and what it releases.

items.meaning: The breakdown of dead plants, dead animals and waste by microorganisms.
A microorganism, such as a bacterium or fungus, that causes decay.
Respiration that uses oxygen to release energy.

items: The microorganisms that cause decay are **bacteria** and **fungi**.
They release enzymes that digest large molecules into small molecules.
They respire, which releases energy and carbon dioxide.
Decay releases mineral ions, such as nitrate and phosphate, into the soil.
Plants take in the mineral ions through their roots and use them to grow, so the materials are recycled.
Bacteria and fungi cause decay.
Decay releases carbon dioxide and mineral ions, which plants use again.

sections.heading: Factors that affect the rate of decay

blocks.text: Temperature, water and oxygen all change how fast the decomposers work.

columns: Effect on the rate of decay
rows: Reactions and enzyme action are faster, and more decomposers are present
Enzymes in the decomposers work too slowly
The enzymes in the decomposers denature
More water gives faster decay, up to a point
Decomposers need water to grow and carry out their reactions
Aerobic respiration needs oxygen to release energy

diagram.alt: A line graph of the rate of decay against temperature. The rate rises slowly at low temperatures, rises steeply to a peak at the optimum temperature, then falls sharply to almost zero as the enzymes denature.

items: In a **compost** heap, soil adds decomposers and turning the contents adds air (oxygen).
Earthworms bring air into the soil, so dead plants decay faster.
Shredding plants gives a larger surface area, so decomposers can feed and respire faster.
In a peat bog, there is little oxygen and the pH is low, so most dead plants do not decay.
Compost and the remains from a **biogas generator** can be spread on fields as a fertiliser, because they release mineral ions.
Food decays when decomposers grow on it.
Preserving food slows decay by removing what the decomposers need.
Keeping food cold slows the enzymes. Drying removes water. Sealing out air removes oxygen.
Decay is fastest when it is warm, moist and there is oxygen.
Too hot denatures the decomposers' enzymes, so decay slows.
Food preservation slows decay by cooling, drying or removing oxygen.

blocks.text: As material decays, its mass falls. The rate of decay is how much mass is lost in each unit of time.

blocks.label: Rate of decay
blocks.formula: rate of decay = change in mass ÷ time taken
where: change in mass, in g (or kg)
rate of decay, in g per day (or kg per day)

diagram.alt: Practice calculating a rate of decay in grams per day from a starting mass, an end mass and a time.
diagram.question: A student puts {start} g of leaves in a compost bin. After {days} days the mass of the leaves is {end} g. Calculate the rate of decay in g per day, to 2 decimal places.
working: Rate of decay = change in mass ÷ time taken, in days.

items: Rate of decay = change in mass ÷ time taken.
Give the unit, such as g per day.

checks.q: Name the two types of microorganism that cause decay.
Explain how an increase in oxygen concentration affects the rate of decay in a compost heap.
checks.a: It increases the rate of decay, because oxygen is needed for aerobic respiration by the bacteria and fungi.

checks.q: Leaves in a compost bin fall in mass from 28.0 g to 20.0 g in 40 days. Calculate the rate of decay.
checks.a: Change in mass = 28.0 − 20.0 = 8.0 g. Rate = 8.0 ÷ 40 = 0.20 g per day.

mistakes.wrong: Decay is caused by viruses, germs or microbes.
mistakes.right: Name the two types of microorganism: bacteria and fungi. Viruses are not accepted, and "microbes" and "germs" are ignored.

mistakes.wrong: The dead plants in a peat bog do not decay because there is no respiration in dead plants.
mistakes.right: "Respiration in dead plants" is not accepted. Write that the microorganisms (bacteria, fungi) lack oxygen for aerobic respiration, so less energy is released.

mistakes.wrong: Respiration produces energy for the microorganisms.
mistakes.right: "Energy produced, made or created" is not accepted. Write that energy is released.

mistakes.wrong: Higher temperature makes the enzymes work better.
mistakes.right: "Work better" is ignored. Write that the enzymes are more active or work more quickly.

worked_example.question:
The rate of decay in a compost heap depends on several environmental factors.

Explain how the rate of decay would be affected by:
- an increase in oxygen concentration
- a temperature increase from 5°C to 25°C
answer_points: Both increase the rate of decay.
Oxygen is needed for aerobic respiration, or oxygen is used to release energy.
Increased temperature causes faster reactions, for example faster respiration or faster enzyme action.
worked_example.tip: The first mark is for saying that both increase the rate. Do not write anaerobic respiration.

exam_phrases: increasing oxygen concentration increases the rate of decomposition because there is more respiration
particles have more (kinetic) energy
rate of enzyme action increases
more decomposers are present
soil introduces microorganisms / decomposers
turning the contents provides oxygen
it is the optimum temperature for the enzymes / bacteria / fungi / decomposers

mistakes.right: 8.5 g is only the change in mass. Divide by the time taken (8.5 ÷ 40), and give the units: grams per day.
The judgement scores one mark. Add the justification: it is the largest percentage decrease in mass, and it is the optimum temperature for the enzymes or decomposers.

worked_example.question:
A student investigated the decomposition of leaves from different types of tree.

The same investigation was extended to include the leaves of a silver birch tree. The starting mass of the leaves was 28.2 grams. After 40 days the mass of the leaves was 19.7 grams.

Calculate the rate of decomposition of the leaves of the silver birch tree.
Give your answer to three significant figures and include the units.
answer_points: Rate = 8.5 ÷ 40 = 0.213 (0.2125 rounded to three significant figures).
worked_example.tip: One mark each for the change in mass, the division and the units.

a larger surface area of dead plants

mistakes.wrong: Holes in the composter let in oxygen, which helps the enzymes to work.
mistakes.right: References to enzymes are ignored here. Write that oxygen is needed by the microbes for aerobic respiration.

mistakes.wrong: The gardener should keep the size of the composter constant.
mistakes.right: "Amount of compost" and "composter size" are ignored. Name a factor that affects the microbes, such as the type, size or mass of the plant material, or the oxygen, and say why.

mistakes.wrong: The loss in mass per week is 16.25 g.
mistakes.right: The question asks for three significant figures: 16.3 g per week.

worked_example.question:
Some students investigate decomposition of dead plant waste. They make a composter from two plastic bottles. They set up bottles with different numbers of air holes. They measure the mass of the bottle and plant waste at the start and after four weeks.

Number of air holes | Mass at the start (g) | Mass after 4 weeks (g)
2 | 300 | 270
4 | 300 | 250
8 | 300 | 240
16 | 300 | 235

Calculate the loss in mass per week of the bottle and plant waste with 16 air holes.
Give your answer to 3 significant figures.
answer_points: To three significant figures: 16.3 g per week.
worked_example.tip: Check the answer line first: 16.3 earns all three marks.
